children: Fortis Healthcare’s facility will offer psychiatric and psychological assessments, treatment and family support for gaming, gambling and related behavioural concerns

Adayu, Fortis Healthcare’s psychiatry and deaddiction hospital, has launched a Behavioural Addiction Clinic in Sector 38, Gurugram, to provide assessment and treatment for gaming, gambling, problematic digital and social media use, and other behavioural patterns affecting daily functioning. The clinic will operate from 9 AM to 10 PM, Monday to Saturday, offering individualised mental healthcare and family support.

The facility will provide psychiatric and psychological assessments, multidisciplinary treatment, individual and family therapy where appropriate, and lifestyle guidance based on each person’s needs. The initiative aims to help individuals whose behavioural patterns interfere with sleep, emotional well-being, relationships, education or work.

The World Health Organization’s International Classification of Diseases (ICD-11) recognises gaming disorder and gambling disorder as disorders due to addictive behaviours. However, frequent digital or social media use does not automatically indicate addiction and requires individual clinical assessment.

Clinical evaluation helps healthcare professionals understand the nature and severity of a concern, identify associated mental health conditions and recommend suitable interventions. Difficulty controlling a behaviour and continuing it despite significant harm can indicate a need for professional support.

Dr. Bishnu Panigrahi, Group Head – Medical Strategy and Operations, Fortis Healthcare, said behavioural addictions and related concerns require careful assessment of their impact on daily life. “Care may involve mental health professionals working together and, where appropriate, supporting family members. Early identification and interventions suited to individual needs can help address difficulties before they become more disruptive,” he said.

Dr. Samir Parikh, Chairperson, Fortis National Mental Health Program and Adayu, emphasised that frequent gaming or digital use should not automatically be classified as addiction. “The concern arises when a person experiences difficulty controlling a behaviour and continues despite significant harm or disruption to daily life,” he said.

He added that clinical assessments consider individual circumstances and functional impact before determining appropriate support. Families can also play an important role in recognising concerns and supporting treatment.

The clinic’s multidisciplinary approach combines clinical assessment, tailored interventions and family involvement where appropriate, with the aim of addressing behavioural concerns and their effects on everyday life.
